chapters.summary: Staff welcomes attendees to the New York City Council hearing on women, gender, and equity, asks everyone to silence electronic devices, and directs those wishing to testify to see the sergeant for an appearance card.
chapters.title: Council staff opens hearing and gives housekeeping instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to the New York City Council hearing on women, gender and equity.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, we're asking everyone to silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And at no point in time, your approach is theirs.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If you wish to testify to this hearing and have a thought appearance card, please see a sergeant at the back for assistance.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, you may begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Amanda Farías opens the hearing, identifies herself as Chair of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, and acknowledges Council Members Aldebol and Santosuosso for joining.
chapters.title: Chair Farías welcomes attendees and acknowledges members present

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Amanda Fetty-S, Chair of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Welcome to today's oversight hearing examining the restructure of the Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence under the Office of Community Safety.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'd like to acknowledge the Councilmembers that are present, Council Members Aldebar and Santos Suoso, who have joined us this morning.

chapters.summary: Farías cites the Cornell University case and the Tompkins County District Attorney reopening a 2024 assault investigation, saying gender-based violence exists in homes, campuses, workplaces, communities, and systems.
chapters.title: Chair Farías frames hearing amid renewed sexual violence allegations

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I want to begin by acknowledging the moment we are in.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Just this week, New Yorkers and women have once again been confronted with the painful realities of sexual violence through the allegations surrounding

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: former Cornell University students and the decision by the Tompkins County District Attorney to reopen the criminal investigation into the 2024 assault and rapes.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: This case has raised renewed public questions about consent, institutional responsibility, and how systems respond when women report violence, and whether our laws and institutions are adequately equipped to protect survivors.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: While that case is outside the jurisdiction of New York City, it is a reminder that gender-based violence does not exist in isolation.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: It exists in our homes, on our campuses, in our workplaces, in our communities, and within the systems that are supposed to protect us.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: And as a city, we are in a pivotal moment.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: We have an opportunity and a responsibility to ensure that preventing and responding to gender-based violence remains a central priority for our government

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: and that survivors can access meaningful support and that our systems are coordinated, accountable, and equipped to respond to the realities women and gender expansive.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: people face.

chapters.summary: Farías describes the Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence as created to treat domestic and gender-based violence as a systemic problem, chairing the Domestic Violence Fatality Review Committee, co-leading the Domestic Violence Task Force, and operating five Family Justice Centers.
chapters.title: Chair Farías recounts NGBV history and role

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence, or NGBV, was created to tackle domestic and gender-based violence as a systemic problem and recognize it as an important issue impacting people across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Since its establishment, NGBV has been a leader in efforts across the city to assess and respond to domestic and gender-based violence.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: These efforts include chairing Domestic Violence Fatality Review Committee, co-leading the Mayor's Domestic Violence Task Force in collaboration with the Mayor's Office of Criminal Justice, and operating the city's five family justice centers, just to name a few.

chapters.summary: Farías asks how restructuring NGBV under the Office of Community Safety can strengthen rather than diminish the city's ability to prevent gender-based violence, support survivors, and hold systems accountable.
chapters.title: Chair Farías poses core question on restructuring NGBV under OCS

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: So today, as we examine the proposed restructuring of NGBV under the Office of Community Safety, I want us to focus on a fundamental question.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: How do we ensure that this restructuring strengthens, not diminishes, the city's ability to prevent gender-based violence, support survivors, and hold our systems accountable?

chapters.summary: Farías introduces Intro 1079, sponsored by herself, which would require NGBV to report anonymous high-level information about calls received by its hotline for survivors of domestic and gender-based violence.
chapters.title: Chair Farías introduces hotline reporting bill Intro 1079

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The committee will also consider the following legislation.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Intro 1079, sponsored by myself, in relation to reporting on a hotline for survivors of gender-based violence.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The bill would require NGBV to report anonymous, high-level information about calls received by NGBV's hotline for survivors of domestic and gender-based violence.

chapters.summary: Farías presents Resolution 441 declaring November 25 as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women in honor of the Mirabal sisters.
chapters.title: Chair Farías introduces Resolution 441 on International Day for Elimination of Violence Against Women

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: We will also hear Resolution 441, also sponsored by me, declaring November 25th as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women in Honor of the Medival Sisters.

chapters.summary: Farías introduces Intro 295, sponsored by Councilmember Lewis, requiring the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to establish a menstrual health program for endometriosis and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
chapters.title: Chair Farías introduces Intro 295 on endometriosis and PMOS screening

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Additionally, we will hear Intro 295, sponsored by...

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Councilmember Farrell-Lewis in relation to establishing a screening program for endometriosis and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.

chapters.summary: Lewis says the bill would require DOHMH screening, referrals, education, and support, cites CDC data on endometriosis and PCOS, explains the 2026 renaming to PMOS, and urges support for Intro 295-A.
chapters.title: Chair Farías reads Councilmember Lewis statement supporting Intro 295

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'll now read a statement from Councilmember Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Farias, for your leadership on and for moving Introduction 295 forward today.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Intro 295 would require the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to establish a menstrual health program providing

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: screening, referrals, and education and support for endometriosis and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, or PMOS.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: It would also expand the city's sexual and reproductive health outreach to include these conditions.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The need is significant.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Federal data from the CDC shows that among women ages 20 to 49, 6.2% has been diagnosed with endometriosis and 8.7% with PCOS in 2022 and 2023.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Among women diagnosed with either condition, rates of current fertility problems were substantially higher than among women without these diagnoses.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Here in New York City, our own Department of Health recognizes that both conditions can cause significant symptoms, including painful or irregular periods, infertility, fatigue, and other health complications.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Yet too many women continue to face gaps in awareness, diagnosis, and access to appropriate care.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: That is why the amendment to recognize PMOS is so important.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: In 2026, the medical community adopted paleoendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome as the new name for the condition previously known as PCOS.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The change reflects a broader understanding

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: that this is a complex endocrine and metabolic condition that affects much more than just the ovaries.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: For too long, women's health needs have been shut out of conversations, research, education, and public health systems that determine whether people receive care.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: We have an opportunity to change that by making accurate information and pathways to

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: to care part of our city's public health infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to support Introduction 295A, and I look forward to continuing the work to ensure that every New Yorker has access to the information, screening, referrals, and support they need to take control of their health.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Farías thanks Lewis, then introduces Resolution 637 sponsored by herself and Councilmember Santosuosso, calling on New York State to require insurers to cover all lactation consultation and counseling services without restrictions.
chapters.title: Chair Farías introduces Resolution 637 on lactation coverage and invites Santosuosso

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I thank Councilmember Lewis for sending in that statement in support of her bill.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Finally, the committee will hear Resolution 637, sponsored by Councilmember Kayla Sanzuzuoso

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: and me, calling on the New York State Legislature to pass and the governor to sign legislation requiring insurers to cover all lactation consultation and counseling services without restrictions and reimburse providers accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'd like to invite Councilmember Sanzuzuoso to make some remarks about this resolution.

chapters.summary: Santosuosso cites breastfeeding benefits, systemic racism and health disparities, federal recognition of lactation consultants, and her own nursing experience, urging the state to ensure insurance coverage without out-of-pocket costs.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso advocates for lactation insurance coverage

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: There is overwhelming evidence that breastfeeding provides a multitude of health benefits to babies and their caregivers.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Difficulties early on often force people to discount breastfeeding, many times without seeking professional advice or support.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Research suggests that many of the disparities are further rooted in systemic racism, which further perpetuates health disparities later in life.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: The U.S.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Department of Health and Human Services has reaffirmed that international board-certified lactation consultants and

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: other professionals are equipped to help parents navigate their challenges with breastfeeding.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: This greatly improves the chance that families will reach their infant feeding goals.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Given the clear health benefits to children and child caregivers, there's no reason that lactation consultation should not be covered by health insurance companies in the state of New York.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: This resolution calls on the governor and state legislature to draft and pass legislation that will ensure all New Yorkers have access to these critical services without having to pay out of pocket.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And as a new mom and as a mom who is nursing, I will just say that nursing can be very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: It requires a lot of support.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: It requires those around you who can help you make sure that it's done effectively.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And it's a shame that all too often these, that consultations and resources are not covered by insurance.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And that's one of the reasons that would-be nursing moms, you know, are not successful in being able to nurse.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And so this resolution is important to me, and I hope that we can get it passed, calling on the state to make sure that insurance is not a reason why a mom cannot choose breastfeeding for herself and for her child.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.title: Chair Farías thanks staff and outlines testimony procedures

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member Sanchez-Suoso.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'd also like to thank committee staff, Julia Goldsmith-Pinkham, Katie Selena, and Allie Stauffer, as well as my own staff, Dan Curtin and Josie McCarris, for their work on today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías

utterances.text: You'll need that.

utterances.text: If you wish to testify on any of the legislation, please indicate that on the witness slip, whether you are here to testify in favor of or in opposition to the legislation.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I also want to point out that we will not be voting on any of the legislation listed today.

utterances.text: To allow as many people to testify as possible, testimony will be limited to two minutes per person, whether you are testifying in person or on Zoom.

utterances.text: I'm also going to ask my colleagues to limit their questions and comments to five minutes.

utterances.text: Please note that witnesses who are here in person will testify before those who are signed onto the Zoom webinar.
