chapters.summary: A Legal Aid staff attorney in the Family Law Domestic Violence Unit says Legal Aid urges keeping NGBV as its own office. He cites City Charter Section 19 classifying domestic violence as a public health issue and says added bureaucracy lessens NGBV's authority and coordination.
chapters.title: Oren Hemovitis testifies for Legal Aid Society on NGBV independence

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: You can begin when ready.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you to Chair Farias and the committee for the opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm speaking today on behalf of the Legal Aid Society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The Legal Aid Society was founded here in New York City in 1876.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We are the oldest and largest provider of legal services in the United States.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We handle some 300,000 cases and legal matters per year for low-income New Yorkers with civil, criminal, and juvenile rights problems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I have been a staff attorney in our Family Law Domestic Violence Unit in our civil practice since 2019.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The Family DV Unit represents survivors of domestic violence in both Supreme and Family Court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: My fellow attorneys and I provide full representation to help survivors assert their rights to custody of their children, to child support and maintenance, to equitable distribution of property, and their right to be safe and free from harm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We urge the Mamdani administration to keep NGBV operating as its own office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: NGBV has been operating for 25 years and has been successful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We strongly believe that independence was a key to that success and that making the office part of OCS will detract from its independence and by extension its mission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: OCS seeks to address community violence with a community-centered model based in restoration and community

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: This goal is commendable and needed, but domestic violence is not a community safety issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The New York City Charter itself, Section 19, the section which established NGBV in the first place, classifies domestic violence as a public health issue, not a community safety issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: NGBV was created and structured with the clear goal of making a focused and streamlined effort to address domestic violence coordinated across city agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The director was appointed by and answered directly to the mayor to give NGBV access to quick decision-making and high authority when needed to facilitate intensive cross-disciplinary focus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Which Section 19 of the City Charter envisioned.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Every layer of bureaucracy which is added between NGBV and the mayor lessens the perceived authority of the office and accordingly the ability of NGBV to work across agency lines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I can personally attest to the success of NGBV.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I've been very familiar with that office through the Family Justice Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Their dedicated and hardworking staff offer survivors of DV a wide range of counseling and services, including legal services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And they send people to me to screen to discuss their cases and give legal advice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: They help other legal service providers also coordinate with agencies to better represent their clients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: On my own cases, I have seen the ease with which

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Agencies can communicate when facilitated by the Family Justice Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: center, and when they coordinate, how they can help provide a systemic answer to a devastating problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I'm concerned about anything which could take away that coordination and communication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Efforts to streamline the city government and reduce bureaucracy are needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But NGBV represents just such an effort, a successful and long-running one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: NGBV already had access to resources and was empowered by the Charter to coordinate with other agencies, and I have personally seen that coordination in action to good effect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Taking away NGBV's independence sends the wrong signal to survivors and those who advocate for survivors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The people of New York City voted to amend the city charter to establish NGBV in 2001 so that the city could have an office that would comprehensively address issues of domestic violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The administration should listen to that mandate and keep NGBV independent from OCS and let it continue succeeding in its mission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you so much for providing testimony today.

chapters.summary: Kim says KAFSC welcomes the new structure and sees value in a connected community safety approach. As a culturally specific organization, KAFSC bridges language, cultural, immigration, and economic barriers and wants to remain a strong partner in shaping the system.
chapters.title: Joanne Kim testifies for Korean American Family Service Center

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: My name is Joanne Kim, and I am the Assistant Director of Community Engagement of the Korean American Family Service Center, or KFSC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: For 37 years, KFSC has supported survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and gender-based violence,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: particularly immigrant survivors who face language, cultural, economic, and immigration-related barriers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Thank you for holding this important hearing and for the opportunity to share KFSC's perspective on the restructuring of the mayor's office to end domestic and gender-based violence under the Office of Community Safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: KAFSC welcomes this new structure and sees real value in a more connected approach to community safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: As a culturally specific organization, our work has never existed in just one category.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: The survivors and families we serve may come to us because of domestic violence, but they are also navigating language barriers, immigration concerns,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: economic insecurity, hate incidents, community safety concerns, and fear of engaging with systems that may not understand their culture or language.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: For organizations like KFSC,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Bringing this work into a broader community safety framework makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: We have deep language capacity and longstanding trust within the communities we serve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: We also know that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: preventing domestic and gender-based violence is closely connected to preventing other forms of violence,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: addressing hate crimes, strengthening community trust, and making sure people know where they can turn before a crisis escalates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: This structure creates an opportunity for greater coordination across these areas while still recognize the specialized expertise that domestic and gender-based violence work requires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: For immigrant communities in particular,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Trusted, culturally specific organizations are often the first point of contact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Survivors may not initially identify what they are experiencing as domestic violence, or they may be hesitant to contact law enforcement or government agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: They may first come to us because they feel unsafe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Because of a family crisis or simply because they need someone who speaks their language and understands their cultural context.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: That is why we believe this broader community safety model has the potential to strengthen the city's response.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: As a new structure continues to develop, we hope culturally specific organizations will

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: remain strong partners in shaping how these systems work on the ground.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Our organizations can help bridge the gap between city systems and communities that have historically been harder to reach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: We look forward to working with the Office of Community Safety, NGBV,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: the city council, and our community partners to make all this new model successful and to ensure that survivors and families receive coordinated, culturally responsive, and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: accessible support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joann Kim
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: Committee on Women and Gender Equity held an oversight hearing on restructuring the Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (NGBV) under the Office of Community Safety (OCS).
Administration officials defended the move and cited $15.7M in new NGBV funding, while advocates and survivors largely opposed the downgrade and demanded survivor-led policymaking.

The committee also heard testimony on bills and resolutions concerning hotline reporting, endometriosis/PMOS screening, International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, and insurance coverage for lactation consultation.
